# Data model

<!-- Generated by `python manage.py data_model_doc` from core/models.py and ledger/models.py. Do not edit by hand;
     run the command after changing a model. tests/test_docs.py fails when this file is stale. -->

This describes what the code stores today. All times are stored in UTC; offset-less input is read
in the contributor's time zone (`Contributor.timezone`), and local times that are ambiguous or
skipped by a daylight-saving change are rejected on import.

## Records, CIDs and corrections

- Every record type below is a `ProvenancedRecord`: it has a `contributor` and a `cid`, and it is
  immutable once saved (`save()` on a stored record, queryset `update()` and `delete()` all raise
  `ImmutableRecordError`). The database enforces it too: row triggers refuse UPDATE and DELETE on
  every record table, `core_supersession` and the ledger tables (migrations `core/0016`,
  `ledger/0002`).
- **CID** = CIDv1, raw codec (0x55), sha2-256, base32 lower case without padding (`bafkrei...`),
  over canonical JSON bytes: `{"contributor": <handle>, "fields": {...}, "kind": <record kind>}`
  with sorted keys, compact separators and UTF-8 (`nymbus/provenance.py`).
- **Fields in the CID:** every concrete field except `id`, `cid`, `contributor` (the handle is in
  the envelope) and `created_at`. Values are coerced to the field type first; decimals are
  quantized to the field's places, so `97.8`, `"97.8"` and `Decimal("97.80")` hash the same;
  datetimes are hashed as UTC ISO strings; naive datetimes are rejected.
- **`OMIT_IF_NULL`:** a field listed there is left out of the canonical content while it is null,
  so records stored before the field existed keep their CID. Every nullable field added after
  records exist must be listed (standing rule, `.kiro/steering/nymbus.md`). Pinned CIDs in the
  tests guard this.
- **Corrections** never edit a record: a new record is saved and a `Supersession` event
  (`old_cid -> new_cid`, same kind and contributor) is appended. A record is *current* when the
  latest Supersession touching its CID points to it, or none does, so a revert (A -> B -> A)
  makes A current again without a new row. Records that point to another record by CID
  (Reset -> ProbeSession, TrainingSet -> TrainingSession) follow the correction chain
  (`core.models.Lineage`).
- Identical content gives the same CID, so re-importing a file is a no-op.

## Export format (nymbus-jsonl, version 1)

First draft of the Nymbus interchange contract. `manage.py export_my_data` and the app's
"Download my data" write one JSON object per line (UTF-8), in the order things were created:

- Line 1: `{"type": "export", "format": "nymbus-jsonl", "version": 1, "contributor": <handle>,
  "timezone": <IANA zone>, "exported_at": <UTC ISO>}`
- Record: `{"type": "record", "kind": <record kind>, "cid": ..., "contributor": <handle>,
  "fields": {...}, "created_at": <UTC ISO>}`. `fields` is exactly the content the CID is computed
  over (OMIT_IF_NULL fields left out while null; datetimes as UTC ISO strings, decimals as strings),
  so `CID(canonical(kind, contributor, fields)) == cid` can be checked from the line alone.
- Correction: `{"type": "supersession", "old_cid": ..., "new_cid": ..., "reason": ..., "created_at": ...}`

`manage.py import_my_data <file>` replays the lines into a database with no records for that
contributor, checks every CID (against the line and against the stored record) and rolls the
whole file back on any error. `created_at` is informational; restored rows get the import time.
The ledger (M5: `grant`, `revocation`, `access_event`) is exported as ordinary record lines after
the records, in replay order (events by `seq`; before each event the grants and revocations whose
`start`/`at` is not after it, a revocation first at equal times), not by `created_at`; the import
replays each access event against the one before it and then runs the full ledger verification.
Not included: Django users, ProbeBaseline settings, module on/off settings.

## Deposit statement (nymbus-statement-jsonl, version 1)

Per local month: line 1 `{"type": "statement", "format": "nymbus-statement-jsonl", "version": 1,
"contributor", "timezone", "month": "YYYY-MM", "unit": "simulated credits", "cid"}`, then
`{"type": "row", "category", "recipient", "purpose", "reads", "records_accessed",
"distinct_records", "units"}` per (category, recipient, purpose) and `{"type": "total", "category",
"reads", "records_accessed", "units"}` per category. `cid` is the CIDv1 of
`canonical("deposit_statement", contributor, {"month", "timezone", "unit", "rows"})` (rows without
`type`). There is no currency field: units are simulated credits.

## Record types

### DailySnapshot (`daily_snapshot`)

| field | type | required | bounds / choices | notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | id | auto |  |  |
| `cid` | text (max 128) | auto |  |  |
| `contributor` | FK -> Contributor | required |  |  |
| `created_at` | datetime (UTC) | auto |  |  |
| `date` | date | required |  |  |
| `sleep_score` | int >= 0 | optional | >= 0; <= 100 |  |
| `bedtime` | datetime (UTC) | optional |  |  |
| `wake_time` | datetime (UTC) | optional |  |  |
| `sleep_duration_min` | int >= 0 | optional | <= 1440 |  |
| `resting_hr_sleep` | int >= 0 | optional | >= 20; <= 150 |  |
| `hrv` | int >= 0 | optional | >= 0; <= 300 |  |
| `spo2` | decimal(4,1) | optional | >= 0; <= 100 |  |
| `weight_kg` | decimal(5,1) | optional | >= 30; <= 300 |  |
| `body_fat_pct` | decimal(4,1) | optional | >= 0; <= 100 |  |
| `skeletal_muscle_kg` | decimal(5,1) | optional |  |  |
| `bmr_kcal` | int >= 0 | optional |  |  |
| `bia_timing` | text (max 16) | default `unknown` | one of: `pre_session`, `post_sauna`, `unknown` |  |
| `source` | text (max 16) | required | one of: `samsung_health`, `seca`, `manual` |  |
| `notes` | text | optional |  |  |

Rules:
- One current snapshot per contributor and `date`; a new one for the same date supersedes it (`record_snapshot`, `save(supersede=True)`).
- `date` must be the local date of `wake_time` in the contributor's time zone.
- `bia_timing = post_sauna` requires `weight_kg`, `body_fat_pct`, `skeletal_muscle_kg` and `bmr_kcal` to be empty.

### WeeklyCheck (`weekly_check`)

Weekly self-rated burnout check. Only the instrument name and score are stored; questionnaire item text is never stored or shipped.

| field | type | required | bounds / choices | notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | id | auto |  |  |
| `cid` | text (max 128) | auto |  |  |
| `contributor` | FK -> Contributor | required |  |  |
| `created_at` | datetime (UTC) | auto |  |  |
| `week_start` | date | required |  | Local Monday of the week. |
| `instrument` | text (max 100) | required |  | Name of the questionnaire used. |
| `score` | decimal(6,2) | required | >= 0 |  |
| `scale_max` | decimal(6,2) | required | >= 0.01 |  |
| `notes` | text | optional |  |  |

Rules:
- `week_start` must be a Monday.
- `score` cannot exceed `scale_max`.
- Only the instrument name and score are stored, never questionnaire item text.

- `session_cid` must be a current TrainingSession of the same contributor.

- `joint_pain_area` requires `joint_pain`. `joint_pain >= 2` is a stop signal in the training report.

### Grant (`grant`)

Permission for one simulated recipient to read one data category, for a stated purpose.

| field | type | required | bounds / choices | notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | id | auto |  |  |
| `cid` | text (max 128) | auto |  |  |
| `contributor` | FK -> Contributor | required |  |  |
| `created_at` | datetime (UTC) | auto |  |  |
| `category` | text (max 64) | required |  |  |
| `recipient` | text (max 32) | required | one of: `self-analysis`, `sim-research-partner` |  |
| `purpose` | text | required |  | Why the recipient may read the data (required). |
| `start` | datetime (UTC) | required |  |  |
| `end` | datetime (UTC) | optional |  | Optional; the grant ends at this time. |

Rules:
- `purpose` must not be blank; `end`, when set, must be after `start` (also a database constraint).
- Active from `start` until `end` (exclusive) and until a Revocation's `at`.
- At most one grant in force per contributor, recipient and category: a grant may not overlap another one's time (until its end or revocation).
- Created through `ledger.service.grant` (known category, contributor lock).

### Revocation (`revocation`)

Ends a grant from `at` on. Supersedes the grant by reference; the grant itself is kept.

| field | type | required | bounds / choices | notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | id | auto |  |  |
| `cid` | text (max 128) | auto |  |  |
| `contributor` | FK -> Contributor | required |  |  |
| `created_at` | datetime (UTC) | auto |  |  |
| `grant_cid` | text (max 128) | required |  | CID of the revoked Grant. |
| `at` | datetime (UTC) | required |  |  |
| `reason` | text (max 200) | optional |  |  |

Rules:
- `grant_cid` must be a Grant of the same contributor; one revocation per grant.

### AccessEvent (`access_event`)

One simulated read under a grant: which records, when, how many simulated credits.

| field | type | required | bounds / choices | notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | id | auto |  |  |
| `cid` | text (max 128) | auto |  |  |
| `contributor` | FK -> Contributor | required |  |  |
| `created_at` | datetime (UTC) | auto |  |  |
| `seq` | int >= 0 | required | >= 1 | 1, 2, ... per contributor. |
| `at` | datetime (UTC) | required |  |  |
| `grant_cid` | text (max 128) | required |  | CID of the Grant the read was made under. |
| `recipient` | text (max 32) | required | one of: `self-analysis`, `sim-research-partner` |  |
| `category` | text (max 64) | required |  |  |
| `purpose` | text | required |  |  |
| `record_cids` | JSON | optional |  | CIDs of the records read (may be empty). |
| `units` | int >= 0 | required |  | Simulated credits (one per record read); not money. |
| `prev_hash` | text (max 64) | required |  | SHA-256 hex of the previous event (64 zeros first). |

Rules:
- Written only by `ledger.service.simulated_read`, after it found an active grant; a refused read writes nothing.
- `recipient`, `category` and `purpose` must match the grant, which must be active at `at`.
- `units` = one simulated credit per record read (`nymbus/ledger.py`); never money.
- Hash chain: `seq` is 1, 2, ... per contributor; `prev_hash` is the SHA-256 of the previous event's canonical bytes (64 zeros for the first). Unique (contributor, seq) and (contributor, prev_hash).
- Grant, Revocation and AccessEvent rows are append-only in the database too (UPDATE/DELETE triggers). `manage.py verify_ledger` recomputes every CID and the chain.
